aboutH2: About the Centre: Rising Sun Treatment Centre in Eel Ground, New Brunswick
intro: The Rising Sun Treatment is a residential treatment for people 18 years or older. There can be 10 people in the treatment at the same time. The program lasts a total of six weeks. There are numerous services provided by the recovery such as assessment, alcohol and drug teaching, case management, client orientation, crisis intervention, professional session, cultural activities, individual counselling, individual and aftercare planning, way of life skills/personal development, group counselling, individual rehab planning, referral, and recreation therapy.

pillars.title: A 10-Bed Centre in Natoaganeg
pillars.body: Rising Sun sits at 31 Riverview Road West in Natoaganeg (Eel Ground First Nation), on the Northwest Miramichi River a short drive from the city of Miramichi. The building has 10 beds in six bedrooms: four rooms with two beds, and two single rooms that share a wheelchair-accessible bathroom. Outside there is a sweat lodge for ceremonies and a land-based camp, and inside a gym with a sauna. The land-based part of the program changes with New Brunswick's four seasons.

pillars.title: Aftercare Planning and Six Months of Follow-Up
pillars.body: Aftercare starts well before graduation. Clients meet one-to-one each week to plan for life after treatment, and the plan is built with their own input. Once you leave, the centre's Continuing Care Counsellor follows up for up to 6 months so nothing falls through the gaps. The Monday night Wellbriety meeting is open to the community as well as current clients, so it is one place former clients can keep coming back to.

pillars.title: Elders, Counsellors and Staff from the Community
pillars.body: An Elder offers cultural teachings and ceremony through the program, and the centre's Elders and knowledge keepers give spiritual guidance. Michael P., an addictions counsellor and cultural practitioner from the Wolastoqwey Nation, is a Pipe Carrier who pours the sweat lodge ceremonies. Several treatment attendants are from Natoaganeg First Nation, the in-house addictions counsellors lead daily sessions, and licensed mental health counsellors come on site twice a week for one-to-one and group work.

overviewH2: Rising Sun Treatment Centre: Center Overview
overview: Rising Sun Treatment Centre opened in 1988 and was listed on this site until 2026 as Rising Sun Rehabilitation Centre. The centre describes its work as culturally and strength-based programs that focus on an alcohol and drug free lifestyle. Its In-House Program follows what it calls a harm reduction-based approach, with individualized care for each person, and daily sessions draw on the Seeking Safety and SMART Recovery programs.

location.heading: Rising Sun Treatment Centre in Eel Ground, New Brunswick
location.intro: Rising Sun is in Natoaganeg (Eel Ground First Nation) on the Northwest Miramichi River, about 10 minutes from the city of Miramichi in northeastern New Brunswick. Moncton is roughly 1 hour 45 minutes away by car and Fredericton about 2 hours, while Bathurst is a little over an hour north and Saint John about 3 hours south.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How long is the program at Rising Sun Treatment Centre?
faqs.a: The main In-House Program runs for six weeks. The centre also runs a 3-week Relapse Prevention Program twice a year, and its 2026 schedule shows those cycles in January and October. Intake dates for each cycle are posted on the centre's homepage, its Apply page and its Facebook page.

faqs.q: How do I apply to Rising Sun?
faqs.a: You send a three-part package: an application form, a medical clearance form filled in by a nurse, nurse practitioner or family doctor, and a medication intake form from your pharmacist or doctor. The centre recommends that a referral agent such as your NNADAP worker, community addictions or outreach counsellor or social worker fills in the application, but family members and the applicant can do it too. Packages are accepted 8 weeks before intake day and should be complete at least 2 to 4 weeks before it.

faqs.q: How much does Rising Sun cost?
faqs.a: Rising Sun does not publish any fees on its website. Ask the intake team at 1-833-444-4626, or your NNADAP or community addictions worker, about costs before you apply. Once you are accepted, the intake team works with you and your referral to arrange medical transportation.

No. Applicants must be detoxed from all psychoactive substances before admission, apart from prescribed opioid agonist therapy, and everyone is drug screened on arrival. If you need withdrawal management, arrange it before your intake date.

faqs.q: Can I attend if I take methadone, Suboxone or Sublocade?
faqs.a: Yes. The centre accepts people prescribed opioid agonist therapy as long as they have been on a stable dose for 3 months before the program starts. It does not accept applicants who are prescribed narcotics or medical marijuana.

faqs.q: What cultural programming does Rising Sun offer?
faqs.a: The centre says an Elder offers cultural teachings and ceremony woven through the program, and its Elders and knowledge keepers give spiritual guidance. There is an on-site sweat lodge for ceremonies, a land-based camp, crafting sessions and a Monday night Wellbriety meeting, a 12-step meeting the centre describes as based in culture and ceremony. The centre aims to help clients keep the best of their Indigenous culture to guide their daily life.

faqs.q: Where is Rising Sun and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Rising Sun is at 31 Riverview Road West in Natoaganeg (Eel Ground First Nation), on the Northwest Miramichi River about 10 minutes from the city of Miramichi. Moncton is about 1 hour 45 minutes away by car, Fredericton about 2 hours and Saint John about 3 hours. Accepted clients arrange travel with the intake team.

Aftercare planning starts during treatment, with weekly one-to-one meetings to prepare for life after graduation. The plan is built with your input, and the Continuing Care Counsellor follows up for up to 6 months after you leave. Former clients can also keep coming to the Monday night Wellbriety meeting, which is open to the community.

Yes. The centre describes itself as a fully accredited 10-bed facility by the Canadian Accreditation Council. The building has six bedrooms, including two single rooms with an adjoining wheelchair-accessible bathroom.

faqs.q: What happens if there is no bed for me?
faqs.a: Rising Sun receives more applications than it has beds each cycle, so it keeps a cancellation list and chooses from it based on priority, need and readiness. If you are not placed, the centre encourages you and your referral to look at other treatment centres listed on its Resources page and to apply again for the next cycle.
